name: Weave
subcategory: patient communications and phone system for healthcare practices
tagline: Unified phone, texting, payments, scheduling and review requests for dental, optometry and veterinary practices.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Weave sells per location via quote and typically bundles hardware phones, so no public sticker price.

verdictSummary: Weave is not an app, it is a phone company wearing a CRM costume. The product is VoIP carrier service, desk handsets, two-way SMS on a real number, card-present payments, and live sync with practice management systems like Dentrix, Eaglesoft and Open Dental. All of that lands in regulated territory: HIPAA for patient data, TCPA for messaging, PCI for payments, plus e911 obligations the moment you answer a phone call. An agent can build you a reminder sender in an afternoon; it cannot build you a telco, a payment processor, or a signed integration with the software that already holds your patient schedule. If you actually run a clinic, this is a buy, not a build.
coreLoopDIY: Reads a CSV export of tomorrow's appointments and fires reminder texts plus a post-visit review request link, logging every send to a local database.
requirements: A Twilio account, a purchased phone number, and A2P 10DLC registration before any real sending
A CSV or read-only database export from your practice management software
Node 20 and a machine that stays awake, or a cheap always-on box for the cron
Written patient consent for SMS, and a legal read on HIPAA and TCPA before it touches real names
Your own Google review link, manually pasted
whatYouLose: The phone system itself: inbound calls, caller pop with patient history, call recording, voicemail transcription, hold music, e911
Live bidirectional sync with the practice management system, so your DIY version is always working from a stale export
Card-present and text-to-pay payments, which means PCI scope you do not want to own
Team inbox behavior: multiple front desk staff seeing who already replied to whom
Deliverability and compliance cover, carrier registration, opt-out handling, audit logs a HIPAA auditor will accept
moatNotes: The integrations moat is quieter than the compliance one but harder to route around: dental PMS vendors do not hand out API keys to hobby projects.
whyPeopleStillPay: Front desk staff do not want six tools, they want one screen that rings, texts, takes a card and knows who is calling. Weave's actual value is that it sits between a legacy practice management database and the phone network, and it is the one that carries the liability when a patient's phone number gets texted the wrong reminder. A clinic owner paying for it is buying a support number to call when the phones go down at 8am, which is exactly the thing a self-hosted script cannot provide. Anything you build yourself becomes your problem at the worst possible moment.
notes: The reminder texts are a weekend build; the phone system, the payment rails and the PMS sync are not. The moat is regulated telco plumbing wired into practice management software nobody else gets keys to.
prompt:
Build a local appointment reminder and review request tool. Single purpose, no login, runs on one machine for one small practice.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/reminders.db
- Twilio Node SDK for SMS
- node-cron inside a separate worker script, not in the Next process

What it does:
1. Import page accepts a CSV upload with columns: patient_name, phone_e164, appointment_at (ISO), provider, visit_type. Upsert into an appointments table keyed on a hash of phone plus appointment_at.
2. Normalize and validate phone numbers, reject anything not E.164. Show rejected rows in a table so they can be fixed and re-uploaded.
3. Two message templates stored in the DB and editable in the UI: a reminder sent 24 hours before the appointment, and a review request sent 3 hours after. Templates support {{patient_name}}, {{provider}}, {{appointment_at_local}} and {{review_link}}.
4. Worker runs every 15 minutes, finds due sends, dispatches via Twilio, writes a row to a message_log table with status, Twilio SID and error text. Never send the same template twice for the same appointment.
5. Handle inbound STOP: a webhook route that records opt-outs in a suppression table and hard-blocks any future send to that number. Show the suppression list in the UI.
6. Dashboard: today's sends, failures, opt-out count, and a searchable message log.

Explicitly out of scope, do not build: inbound voice calls, payments, a team inbox, patient records, PMS integrations, multi-tenant accounts, telemetry.

Rules:
- TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID, TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN, TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER and REVIEW_LINK in .env, with a .env.example. No secrets in code.
- DRY_RUN=true by default: log messages to the console and the DB instead of sending.
- All timestamps stored UTC, displayed in a PRACTICE_TZ from .env.
- Print a README with a blunt warning that this handles patient data, is not HIPAA compliant, and requires A2P 10DLC registration and written consent before sending anything to a real person.
